title: Locked Flaps
tagline: Flaps jammed at 1 on a gusty approach to London City.
history: Inspired by flap failures on approach to short runways, where the higher landing speed turns a routine arrival into a choice between a precise touchdown and a diversion to a longer runway.
situation: Six miles from London City's runway 27 — 1,508 m long, a steep 5.5° glidepath, buildings all round — in a gusty southerly. As you select flap 2 nothing happens: the flaps are locked at 1. Your approach speed just went up by 25 knots.
tips: Vref + 25 kt with flap 1 — London City is very short for that
Southend (05/23, 1,856 m) and Stansted (04/22, 3,049 m) are nearby
Crab into the wind, kick it straight just before touchdown
Full reverse and maximum braking once down

do.note: F/O: Flaps two… they're not moving. Flap fault — locked at one.
ATC: Wind 200 degrees 20 knots, gusting 32. Say intentions.

objectives.text: Land and stop on a runway
